newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's 1996 bauxite exports dip to 400,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's 1996 bauxite exports dip to 400,000 tonnes.

text.p: Ghana's bauxite exports have fallen to 400,000 tonnes this year, down 130,000, but it enters the new year with stocks of more than 200,000 tonnes, a senior official of the Ghana Bauxite Company Ltd (GBC) said.
"The main problem is derailments of trains. This year we missed several ships," deputy director Ben Adoo told Reuters.
"But we are geared up to start a very good 1997. We are in excess of 100,000 tonnes of stock in the port and another 100,000 tonnes at the mine," he said.
Rehabilitated in 1983, the 240-km rail line between the Awaso bauxite mine and Takoradi port needs urgent repairs as well as more regular maintenance, Adoo said.
Bauxite exports had been on the rise in recent years.
From 364,642 tonnes in 1993 and 451,520 in 1994, exports rose to 530,442 tonnes in 1995.
The government owns 55 percent of GBC and Alcan Chemicals Europe, a British-based unit of Alcan Canada, controls the rest.
The government intends to off-load up to 35 percent of its shares by mid-1997, most likely to Alcan, according to Adoo.
"They (Alcan) have great interest. The bulk of the discussion has been done, including the legal framework," he said.
The company aims to increase annual output of the mine to one million tonnes by 2000.
"Mining one million tonnes by 2000 is not a problem. Whoever takes over GBC wants to be sure that Ghana Railways can rail," said Adoo.
For 1997 Ghana Railways has pledged to transport more than 500,000 tonnes, purchase new 40-tonne wagons and repair the tracks, Adoo said.

Half of exports go to Alcan's chemical plant in Edinburgh, Scotland, and 25 percent to Alcan-Quebec. The remaining 25 percent was sold in 1995 to Alusuisse in Switzerland and to a company in Slovakia for blending with lower grade bauxite.
In the medium to long term GBC plans to process part of its bauxite into aluminium-sulphate, used for water treatment, Adoo said.
